summary: Security sign-off for the demo: PASS. There are no blocker or high findings. Every attack from reviews 1 and 2 is still blocked. Every Sprint C fix held up when attacked directly as owner, accountant, sales, operations, anon and an org-B owner: SEC1-03/04/05/06/07/08/09/11/12 and SEC2-05/06/07/08/09/10/11. A Supabase-like NOSUPERUSER BYPASSRLS owner with Supabase default privileges runs the whole demo flow, CI passes, and anon can do nothing. Open: SEC3-03 (major, dev1: Plant buyers list shows every buyer as Paid after A6), SEC3-01 (minor, dev1: follow_ups UPDATE lets staff postpone or rewrite other people's and system reminders), SEC3-02 (minor, dev2: no guard that the migration owner bypasses RLS; under NOBYPASSRLS the whole app recurses), SEC3-04 (minor, dev1: seed-users falls back to the public demo password on hosted), plus 3 info items.

findings.problem: After A6, v_money_due is empty for operations, but the buyers list still shows a money fact and pill for every buyer, so Plant sees every buyer as ₹0 · Paid, including the buyer whose $18,900 is late. buyers/[id] already hides money with isPlant.
findings.fix: In buyers/page.tsx set isPlant = profile.role === 'operations' and, for Plant, render no money fact2/badge and skip the overdue sort; in queries.ts skip the v_money_due read for operations.

findings.problem: follow_ups_update only checks org + module, so any user holding the module can PATCH note/due_on on anyone's reminder, including system reminders. Sales pushed 'Balance $18,900 due' to 2099 (owner Home to-do 5 -> 3) and rewrote the owner's note to 'Owner says: OK to go below floor'. This undoes the A9/SEC2-11 delete protection. It is audited, and no app path updates follow_ups.
findings.fix: Add AND (fn_user_role() = 'owner' OR (follow_ups.created_by = auth.uid() AND follow_ups.done_by IS NULL)) to both USING and WITH CHECK of follow_ups_update (keep the buyer same-org check); add a Vitest case: sales UPDATE of the Balance reminder -> 0 rows, own reminder -> 1 row.

findings.problem: Nothing checks that the migration/function owner is SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS. Under a NOBYPASSRLS owner every request fails with stack depth limit exceeded (fn_current_org -> profiles policy -> fn_current_org), and the 0007 audit scrub silently touches 0 rows. Supabase documents postgres as bypassrls, so this is a credentials-day guard, not a live bug.
findings.fix: Top of 0007: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT (SELECT rolsuper OR rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'migration owner % must be SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS', current_user; END IF; END $$; add CI check 11: every SECURITY DEFINER function owner has rolsuper OR rolbypassrls.

findings.problem: With Supabase keys set and DEMO_PASSWORD empty, the four real hosted accounts (owner included) are created with the public DemoPass123!, which is in the repo and docs. The script only warns, and after DEMO_MODE=false the logins stay open to anyone who read the repo.
findings.fix: In the Supabase branch, exit 1 with 'Set DEMO_PASSWORD in .env.local before creating Supabase users' when process.env.DEMO_PASSWORD is empty; drop the fallback there (the local shim does not use this path).

findings.problem: fn_payment_record refuses future dates but accepts any past date (accountant receipt dated 1900-01-01 was accepted).
findings.fix: Optional: raise bad_payload received_on when p_received_on < order created_at::date - 365.

findings.problem: A6 covers payments, balances and KPIs only. Through the API Plant still reads orders.total/advance_expected, 5 quotes, 4 items with floor_price_at_time, and follow-up note text such as 'Balance $18,900 due' (also shown on Plant Home To do).
findings.fix: Lead decision. If 'Plant reads no money' must be literal, expose orders to operations through a column-limited view and add fn_user_role() IS DISTINCT FROM 'operations' to the quotations/quotation_items SELECT policies.

findings.problem: npm test against a Supabase-like non-superuser DB gives 11 failed / 100 passed (session_replication_role needs a superuser; gen_salt lives in extensions, so 42883 instead of 42501). These are harness assumptions, not product defects.
findings.fix: Keep tests local-only (README already says so); optionally skip those assertions when current_user is not a superuser.

blocked_waiting_for_credentials: Hosted: SELECT rolsuper, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user on the migration connection (expect f | t), then npm run ci:tenant-check against the hosted DATABASE_URL
Web login end to end (password and Try as) with GoTrue cookies, middleware cookie refresh
PostgREST over HTTP: anon key calls to /rest/v1 tables and /rpc definers (expect 401/42501)
Signed-in receipt view and print, stepper dates on screen
usability_notes: Plant buyers list shows every buyer as Paid (SEC3-03); this is visible in the demo if Plant opens Buyers.
Plant Home 'To do today' shows money text from follow-up notes ('Balance $18,900 due') although A6 hides money from Plant.

Seeded plain notes have done_by set, so their authors cannot delete them (A9 requires done_by IS NULL); only notes made in the app are deletable by their author. There is no delete button for notes in the UI today, so this is not visible.
While DEMO_MODE=true anyone with the URL can sign in as owner; run npm run db:seed to restore the demo story after rehearsals, and follow hosted-supabase.md section 6 after the demo.
